items.title: The deal I lost on my own
items.excerpt: A managing director agreed everything and it still never moved. Nobody beat me on it. Here is what I missed, and what I look for now.
items.author: Scott Robinson
items.body:
Early in my career at Ford I had a managing director who wanted to change his entire fleet. Priced, specified, agreed. It never moved.

I had been taught to sell to the man who signs the cheque, so that is exactly what I did. His service team, his finance people and his management all had their own reasons to stay where they were. He was never going to make his own staff unhappy to please me.

Nobody beat me on that deal. I lost it on my own.

## It is not a rare way to lose

In a [2022 Harvard Business Review article](https://hbr.org/2022/06/stop-losing-sales-to-customer-indecision), Matthew Dixon and Ted McKenna report on more than 2.5 million recorded sales conversations. Between 40% and 60% of deals ended up lost to customers who expressed their intent to purchase and then failed to act. The study spans transactional and complex sales across the board rather than industrial sales in particular, and it comes from the authors' own book on the subject, so read it with that in mind.

Gartner measured what goes on inside buying groups. In a [survey of 632 B2B buyers, published in May 2025](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-05-07-gartner-sales-survey-finds-74-percent-of-b2b-buyer-teams-demonstrate-unhealthy-conflict-during-the-decision-process), 74% of buyer teams demonstrated unhealthy conflict during the decision. In the same May 2025 release, Delainey Kirkwood of Gartner puts those groups at five to 16 people across as many as four functions.

That is the argument you are not in. It happens while you are sat at your desk waiting for an answer.

## Same problem, twenty years later

On a £1.9M job through Técnicas Reunidas exactly the same thing was happening. Technical signed off, documentation agreed, terms sat there going nowhere.

The difference was that by then I knew whose room the decision was actually in. So I stopped guessing at it through the contractor. I booked a call with Aramco and mapped the timings from the owner's side.

## What I look for now

This is [the decision map](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/#method), and when a deal goes quiet I want three answers.

Where does the decision actually live? Not who signs. Who has to be comfortable before anybody signs.

Who is arguing against you, and what is their reason? Most of the reasons belong to the business, not the person in front of you.

What have you put in your champion's hands? They are the one having that argument without you.

## The short version

If a deal has gone quiet, find out whether it is being argued about in a room you are not in. Find the room, find who is arguing, and arm the person fighting your corner.

Got one that has stopped? [Bring a stalled deal](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/stalled-deal-review/). Thirty minutes on one deal, no charge, and you leave knowing where it has actually stopped and the three things to do next.

## Sources

- Harvard Business Review, "Stop Losing Sales to Customer Indecision", 2022. https://hbr.org/2022/06/stop-losing-sales-to-customer-indecision
- Gartner, "Gartner Sales Survey Finds 74% of B2B Buyer Teams Demonstrate Unhealthy Conflict During The Decision Process", 2025. https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-05-07-gartner-sales-survey-finds-74-percent-of-b2b-buyer-teams-demonstrate-unhealthy-conflict-during-the-decision-process

items.title: Technical gets you in. Procurement decides whether you get paid.
items.excerpt: Three gates sit between you and the order. Win the first and lose either of the other two and you have worked eighteen months for nothing.
items.author: Scott Robinson
items.body:
Technical gets you into the engine build. Quality decides whether you stay in it. Procurement decides whether you get paid.

Win the first and lose either of the other two and you have worked eighteen months for nothing.

The first gate is the easy one to enjoy. An engineer wants to talk about the product. You want to talk about the product. You can go home thinking it is going well.

## Procurement is not waiting at the end

[Forrester's 2026 report on business buying](https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2026-the-state-of-business-buying/) says procurement professionals are decision makers in 53% of buying cycles and engage from the start of the process. That comes from a press release that does not state the sample or break it down by industry, so treat it as a direction rather than a measurement.

The same release puts the typical decision at 13 internal stakeholders and nine external influencers. [Delainey Kirkwood of Gartner, in a May 2025 release](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-05-07-gartner-sales-survey-finds-74-percent-of-b2b-buyer-teams-demonstrate-unhealthy-conflict-during-the-decision-process), says five to 16 people across as many as four functions. Forrester lists outside influencers separately and that Gartner release does not say whether its figure includes them, so there is no single right number. The point is that it is a lot more people than the engineer you were talking to.

## Three gates, three different conversations

Treat them as three separate sales inside one deal. That is what [the decision map](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/#method) is for.

**Technical.** What do they need to see before they will put their name to it?

**Quality.** What would make them take you out once you are in? Ask it while things are going well.

**Procurement.** What do they need in order to justify the proposal? Not the discount. The justification.

On Marjan, the technical work was done and the documentation was agreed, and the terms were still hanging. Being technically through did not move it. Finding out from the owner when they actually wanted units on site did.

## The short version

Win all three gates or you have not won. If you can only name the person at one of them, you know where to spend next week.

Got one that has stopped at a gate? [Bring a stalled deal](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/stalled-deal-review/). Thirty minutes on one deal, no charge, and you leave knowing where it has actually stopped and the three things to do next.

## Sources

- Forrester, "Forrester's 2026 Buyer Insights: GenAI Is Upending B2B Buying As Leaders Face Mounting Pressure To Justify Every Dollar Spent", 2026. https://www.forrester.com/press-newsroom/forrester-2026-the-state-of-business-buying/
- Gartner, "Gartner Sales Survey Finds 74% of B2B Buyer Teams Demonstrate Unhealthy Conflict During The Decision Process", 2025. https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-05-07-gartner-sales-survey-finds-74-percent-of-b2b-buyer-teams-demonstrate-unhealthy-conflict-during-the-decision-process

items.title: Being in the spec helps. It is not the whole job.
items.excerpt: The specification is the biggest lever on a project. It is not pass or fail, and treating it that way costs sellers winnable work.
items.author: Scott Robinson
items.body:
Being specified is the single biggest lever in project sales. It tilts the odds hard in your favour and I would always rather be in than out.

It is not pass or fail.

Thousands of projects are won by manufacturers who are on the approved vendor list and not written into the specification. It depends on the EPC, the operator, the budget and the commercial case. Treat being outside the spec as the end of the job and you either walk away from winnable business or spend six months pushing at the wrong door.

## A specification is a position, not an order

Hughes were in the ADNOC and Aramco specifications fifteen years before I joined. In 2024 I increased Middle East sales by 167% on the year before.

I am not going to tell you a story about what happened in those fifteen years, because I was not there. The two facts are enough for this. Being written in gives you a position. Somebody still has to go and sell from it.

## Work both angles

On Marjan I booked a call with Aramco and mapped the timings from the owner's side. Nobody else did it, because everybody else was working the EPC. If you only work the contractor, you are guessing at the dates.

That is why [both angles](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/#method) is part of the method, and it matters most when you are outside the spec. The contractor will tell you what the specification says. The owner can tell you what they actually want and when they actually want it.

## The questions to ask before you walk away

Are you on the approved vendor list, or could you be in the time available?

Which EPC holds this, and how much room do they have?

What does the operator actually care about on this job?

Is there budget, and whose is it?

What is the commercial case for changing, stated in terms somebody can defend in a meeting you will not be in?

Some of the time those answers tell you to leave it alone, and that is a good result if you get it in a fortnight rather than a year.

## The short version

The specification is the biggest lever and it is still only a lever. Ask the five questions before you decide the job has gone.

Outside the spec on one right now? [Bring a stalled deal](https://ringcraftcoaching.com/stalled-deal-review/). Thirty minutes on one deal, no charge, and you leave knowing where it has actually stopped and the three things to do next.
